rationale: dual_domain_bilateral_n2i-claude-agentic: warm_start=True, pretrain_epochs=2, train_n=400, n_iter=30, val_n=200, batch_size=1, grad_clip=1.0, lr=0.005, proj_n_bf=1, img_n_bf=1, img_sr=0.0002, img_kernel=5, outer_wall_s=900, seed=42, rationale=iter-10 dual_domain_bilateral_n2i, ONE-KNOB: image BF KERNEL img_kernel 7->5 (tighter spatial window), on iter-7 CHAMPION base (img_sr=0.0002, img_sx=img_sy=1.5 default, n_iter=30). Spatial sigma REVERTED to default 1.5 (iter-9 widen 1.5->2.5 gave hr=0.1140 < champ 0.1261 -> widening blurs fibroglandular detail; spatial axis does NOT want to widen). CHAMPION = iter-7 hr=0.1261 SSIM0.9606 (val_n=200). HYPOTHESIS: iter-9 showed breast fine structure is DAMAGED by a wider spatial support -> the recon wants the SHARPEST possible spatial averaging. A 5x5 kernel (vs 7x7) confines the BF to immediate neighbours, denoising flat noise while preserving the finest fibroglandular edges better than 7x7 -> hr could edge above 0.1261. If FLAT/DROP, 7x7 is already fine (the tight range sigma, not the window, sets edge-preservation) and kernel is neutral. SECONDARY BENEFIT: 5x5 unfold is FASTER than 7x7 -> keeps the per-image loop under outer_wall_s=900 so val_n stays a clean 200 (iters 8/9 trimmed to 193 under heavier configs, confounding hr). BUDGET: smaller kernel -> ~700-900s, no wall trim expected. ONE knob: img_kernel 7->5.
